problem:
Let $V=C[-1,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-1,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-1}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=1-t.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Norm of a Vector in Inner Product Spaces

feedback.problem:
Let $V=C[-\pi ,\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\,{sin}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{t}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}{4}){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi }{4})-(-\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\pi )}{4}) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identity 

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡t=\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
